name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY)
short_description: Voluntary contributory pension for small and marginal farmers: Rs 3,000 per month after age 60.
full_description: An old age pension scheme for landholding small and marginal farmers (cultivable land up to 2 hectares as per state land records) who join between 18 and 40 years of age. The farmer contributes Rs 55 to Rs 200 per month depending on entry age until age 60, the Central Government makes an equal matching contribution, and LIC manages the pension fund. After death of a pensioner the spouse receives 50% as family pension. Excluded: farmers covered by NPS, ESIC, EPFO or who opted for PM-SYM / NPS-Traders, income tax payers, registered professionals, and serving or retired government officers (MTS/Class IV/Group D exempted).
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
benefit_description: Minimum assured pension of Rs 3,000 per month from age 60; matching government contribution during the contribution period.
documents: Aadhaar card | Savings bank account details (or PM-KISAN account) | Land records showing up to 2 hectares | Mobile number
apply_steps: Visit the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) or contact the State PM-KISAN Nodal Officer | Provide Aadhaar and bank details for enrolment | Sign the enrolment-cum-auto-debit mandate (contribution can be auto-debited from PM-KISAN benefits) | Receive the Kisan Pension Account Number

name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) with Modified Interest Subvention
short_description: Short-term crop and allied-activity credit for farmers at 7% interest, effectively 4% on prompt repayment.
full_description: The Kisan Credit Card provides farmers timely short-term credit for cultivation, post-harvest and allied activities. Under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS), KCC loans carry a concessional 7% interest rate and farmers who repay promptly receive up to 3% Prompt Repayment Incentive, bringing the effective rate to 4%. Owner-cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers, SHGs/JLGs of farmers, and fishers and animal husbandry farmers are covered. A 2026 PIB document states the MISS loan limit has been enhanced to Rs 5 lakh with collateral-free credit up to Rs 2 lakh; banks apply their own appraisal.
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
benefit_description: Concessional crop/allied loan at 7% (effective 4% with prompt repayment); limit based on scale of finance and landholding.
documents: KCC application form | Identity proof (Aadhaar) | Address proof | Land records or tenancy/lease documents | For fishers: pond/vessel ownership or lease and licence | Passport-size photographs
apply_steps: Approach a commercial bank, regional rural bank, small finance bank or cooperative bank | Fill the KCC application form | Submit land/cultivation or fisheries/animal husbandry documents | Bank appraises and sanctions the credit limit and issues the card

name: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
short_description: Central subsidy of up to Rs 78,000 for installing rooftop solar on your own house.
full_description: Rooftop solar programme for residential households launched in February 2024. Central Financial Assistance is Rs 30,000 per kW for the first 2 kW and Rs 18,000 for the third kW, capped at Rs 78,000 for systems of 3 kW and above. Applicant must be an Indian citizen owning a house with a roof suitable for solar panels, have a valid electricity connection, and must not have availed any other solar subsidy. Collateral-free concessional loans are available through public sector banks.
ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
benefit_description: Rs 30,000 (1 kW), Rs 60,000 (2 kW), Rs 78,000 (3 kW or more) credited to the bank account after installation and DISCOM inspection.
documents: Latest electricity bill | Proof of house/roof ownership | Aadhaar | Bank account details and cancelled cheque
apply_steps: Register on pmsuryaghar.gov.in selecting your state and electricity distribution company | Apply for rooftop solar and obtain DISCOM feasibility approval | Install the system through a registered vendor | Apply for net metering; DISCOM inspects and issues the commissioning certificate | Submit bank details and cancelled cheque to receive the subsidy

name: PM YASASVI Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
short_description: Post-matric scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT students with family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh.
full_description: Under PM Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for a Vibrant India (PM YASASVI), the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment funds post-matric scholarships (Class 11 onwards, including degree and postgraduate courses) for OBC, Economically Backward Class and De-notified Tribe students whose parents' or guardians' annual income from all sources does not exceed Rs 2.5 lakh. It is implemented through state governments and disbursed by DBT.
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
benefit_description: Maintenance allowance and fee reimbursement as per course group and state norms.
documents: Caste certificate (OBC/EBC/DNT) | Family income certificate from competent authority | Previous year mark sheet | Fee receipt / admission proof | Aadhaar-seeded bank account
apply_steps: Register on the National Scholarship Portal or your state scholarship portal | Fill the post-matric application for OBC/EBC/DNT | Upload income, caste and academic documents | Institute and district verify the application | Scholarship is paid by DBT

name: National Overseas Scholarship for SC Students
short_description: Funding for Master's and PhD study at top-500 QS-ranked foreign universities for SC students.
full_description: Central sector scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment that funds Scheduled Caste students (and some denotified/landless labourer categories) for Master's and PhD courses abroad. 125 fresh awards per selection year, subject to funds. Applicants must be below 35 years as on 1 April of the selection year, have total family income up to Rs 8 lakh per year, and hold an unconditional admission offer from a top-500 QS ranked foreign institution.
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
benefit_description: Tuition fees, maintenance allowance, visa fee, air passage and other allowances as per scheme guidelines.
documents: SC caste certificate | Family income certificate from revenue authority | Unconditional admission offer letter | Mark sheets (60% in qualifying exam) | Age proof | Passport
apply_steps: Register on the NOS portal during the selection-year window | Fill the application and upload documents | Ministry selects candidates as per merit and slots | Selected candidates receive award letter and complete formalities

name: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)
short_description: Cash assistance to pregnant women for delivering in a government or accredited health facility.
full_description: Safe motherhood intervention under the National Health Mission. In Low Performing States (Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Assam, Rajasthan, Odisha, Jammu and Kashmir) all pregnant women delivering in government health centres are eligible. In High Performing States only BPL and SC/ST women are eligible. BPL and SC/ST women delivering in accredited private institutions are eligible in all states.
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
benefit_description: Mother's package for institutional delivery: LPS rural Rs 1,400, LPS urban Rs 1,000, HPS rural Rs 700, HPS urban Rs 600.
documents: MCP / JSY card | Aadhaar | Bank account details | BPL card or SC/ST certificate (where required) | Delivery record from the health facility
apply_steps: Register the pregnancy with the ASHA, ANM or nearest government health centre | Obtain the JSY / MCP card | Deliver at a government or accredited health facility | Cash assistance is paid to the mother's bank account

name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
short_description: Collateral-free business loans up to Rs 10 crore for micro and small enterprises, backed by a government guarantee.
full_description: The Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises guarantees collateral-free credit extended by member lending institutions to new and existing micro and small enterprises. With effect from 1 April 2025 guarantees are available for credit up to Rs 10 crore. Udyam Registration is mandatory. Guarantee coverage is 75% to 90% depending on loan size and borrower category (higher for women-led enterprises and the North East). A guarantee fee is payable.
ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
benefit_description: Collateral-free and third-party-guarantee-free term loan / working capital up to Rs 10 crore through banks and NBFCs.
documents: Udyam Registration Certificate | Business plan / project report | KYC of promoters | Bank statements | Financial statements (existing units)
apply_steps: Obtain Udyam Registration | Apply for a business loan at a CGTMSE member bank or NBFC | Lender appraises the proposal and seeks guarantee cover from CGTMSE | Loan sanctioned without collateral

name: PM-Vidyalaxmi Education Loan Scheme
short_description: Collateral-free, guarantor-free education loans for students admitted on merit to top institutions, with 3% interest subvention for family income up to Rs 8 lakh.
full_description: Launched in November 2024, PM-Vidyalaxmi provides collateral-free and guarantor-free education loans to students admitted on merit (not management/NRI quota) to designated Quality Higher Education Institutions. The Government guarantees 75% of defaults on loans up to Rs 7.5 lakh. Students with annual family income up to Rs 8 lakh who are not availing any other scholarship or interest subvention get 3% interest subvention on loans up to Rs 10 lakh during the moratorium period (up to one lakh fresh students a year). Interest is capped at the bank's EBLR + 0.5%.
ministry: Ministry of Education
benefit_description: Collateral-free education loan; 3% interest subvention on up to Rs 10 lakh for family income up to Rs 8 lakh.
documents: Admission letter from a designated QHEI | Fee structure | Aadhaar and PAN | Family income certificate (for interest subvention) | Academic mark sheets | Bank account details
apply_steps: Register on the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal | Fill the Common Education Loan Application Form | Choose up to three banks and apply | Track and accept the sanctioned loan on the portal | Apply for interest subvention through the portal if eligible

name: Central Sector Scheme of Scholarships for College and University Students
short_description: Rs 12,000 to Rs 20,000 per year for students above the 80th percentile in Class 12 with family income below Rs 4.5 lakh.
full_description: Ministry of Education scholarship (part of PM-USP) for students above the 80th percentile of successful candidates in their Class 12 board in the relevant stream, pursuing regular degree courses, with gross parental income below Rs 4.5 lakh per year. Up to 82,000 fresh scholarships a year, split equally between boys and girls. Rs 12,000 per annum for the first three years and Rs 20,000 per annum for the fourth and fifth years (professional / postgraduate).
ministry: Ministry of Education
benefit_description: Rs 12,000 per year (years 1-3), Rs 20,000 per year (years 4-5), paid by DBT.
documents: Class 12 mark sheet | Family income certificate | Admission proof / bonafide certificate | Aadhaar-seeded bank account
apply_steps: Register on the National Scholarship Portal | Apply under 'Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students' | Upload documents | Institute and state board verify | Scholarship credited by DBT; renew yearly

name: Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids and Appliances (ADIP)
short_description: Free or subsidised assistive devices for persons with 40%+ disability and income up to Rs 30,000 per month.
full_description: Under the ADIP scheme of the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Indian citizens with a benchmark disability (40% or more) and monthly income from all sources not exceeding Rs 30,000 receive aids and appliances such as tricycles, wheelchairs, hearing aids and prosthetics. Motorised tricycles/wheelchairs (up to Rs 50,000) are for persons with 80%+ severe disability, with full subsidy up to Rs 22,500 monthly income and 50% subsidy up to Rs 30,000. Persons who received similar assistance in the previous 3 years are not eligible.
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (DEPwD)
benefit_description: Aids and appliances free or at 50% cost depending on income; distributed through ALIMCO and implementing agencies.
documents: Disability certificate / UDID card (40% or more) | Income certificate | Aadhaar | Address proof | Passport-size photograph
apply_steps: Register on the ADIP/ARJUN portal or attend an assessment camp | Get assessed by medical/rehabilitation experts | Submit income and disability documents | Receive the appliance at a distribution camp

name: Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (SCSS)
short_description: Government-backed 5-year savings scheme for people aged 60+ with quarterly interest, deposits up to Rs 30 lakh.
full_description: Small savings scheme of the Ministry of Finance available at post offices and authorised banks. Individuals aged 60 or above can open an account; those who retired between 55 and 60 can open one within one month of receiving retirement benefits (amount limited to those benefits); defence retirees have separate relaxation. Maximum deposit Rs 30 lakh across all SCSS accounts, tenure 5 years extendable by 3 years, interest paid quarterly at the rate notified each quarter. NRIs are not eligible.
ministry: Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs)
benefit_description: Government-notified interest rate (revised quarterly) paid every quarter on deposits of Rs 1,000 to Rs 30 lakh.
documents: SCSS account opening form | Aadhaar | PAN | Age proof | Retirement benefit proof / certificate (if aged 55-60) | Photographs
apply_steps: Visit a post office or authorised bank branch | Submit the account opening form with KYC | Deposit by cash (below Rs 1 lakh) or cheque/NEFT | Receive quarterly interest into your linked account

name: National Pension Scheme for Traders and Self-Employed Persons (NPS-Traders)
short_description: Contributory pension of Rs 3,000 per month after 60 for shopkeepers, traders and self-employed aged 18-40.
full_description: Voluntary contributory pension scheme of the Ministry of Labour and Employment for retail traders, shopkeepers and self-employed persons aged 18 to 40 at entry with annual turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore. The subscriber's monthly contribution (fixed by entry age) is matched by the Central Government. Income tax payers and members of NPS (government-funded), ESIC, EPFO or PM-SYM are not eligible. Spouse receives 50% as family pension.
ministry: Ministry of Labour and Employment
benefit_description: Minimum assured pension of Rs 3,000 per month after age 60; equal matching contribution by the Government.
documents: Aadhaar card | Savings bank or Jan Dhan account details | Mobile number
apply_steps: Visit the nearest Common Service Centre (find via locator.csccloud.in) or self-enrol on maandhan.in | Authenticate with Aadhaar and give bank details | Pay the first contribution | Sign the auto-debit mandate for monthly contributions

name: Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Tribe Students
short_description: Scholarship for ST students in Class 11 and above with parental income up to Rs 2.5 lakh.
full_description: Centrally sponsored scheme of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, implemented through state and UT governments, supporting Scheduled Tribe students studying in Class 11 and above (including diploma, degree, postgraduate and professional courses) whose parental income is not more than Rs 2.5 lakh per annum. Open-ended: all eligible students are covered.
ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
benefit_description: Compulsory fee reimbursement and maintenance allowance as per course group and state norms.
documents: ST certificate | Parental income certificate | Previous mark sheet | Admission / fee receipt | Aadhaar-seeded bank account
apply_steps: Apply on your state's scholarship portal or the National Scholarship Portal | Upload ST, income and academic documents | Institute and state tribal welfare department verify | Scholarship paid by DBT

name: Gruha Lakshmi Scheme
short_description: Rs 2,000 per month to the woman head of household on a Karnataka ration card.
full_description: Karnataka government guarantee scheme paying Rs 2,000 per month to the woman identified as head of household (yajamani) on an Antyodaya, BPL or APL ration card. One woman per family. Excluded: women who are government employees or pensioners, and families where the woman or her husband pays income tax or files GST returns.
ministry: Department of Women and Child Development, Government of Karnataka
benefit_description: Rs 2,000 per month by DBT to an Aadhaar-seeded bank account.
documents: Ration card naming the woman as head of household | Aadhaar of applicant and husband | Aadhaar-seeded bank account | Mobile number
apply_steps: Apply on the Seva Sindhu portal or at Karnataka One / Bangalore One / Grama One centres | Enter ration card and Aadhaar details | Submit self-declaration | Benefit credited monthly after verification

name: Yuva Nidhi Scheme
short_description: Unemployment allowance of Rs 3,000/month for graduates and Rs 1,500/month for diploma holders in Karnataka.
full_description: Karnataka guarantee scheme for graduates and diploma holders (year of passing 2023 or later) who remain unemployed for 180 days after passing. Applicants must be Karnataka domicile (studied in the state for at least 6 years up to degree/diploma). Paid for up to two years or until employment. Not eligible: those pursuing higher studies, receiving apprenticeship stipend, employed, self-employed with a bank loan, or receiving similar unemployment assistance.
ministry: Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood, Government of Karnataka
benefit_description: Rs 3,000 per month for graduates / Rs 1,500 per month for diploma holders, up to 2 years.
documents: Degree or diploma certificate | Proof of 6 years of study in Karnataka | Aadhaar | Aadhaar-seeded bank account | Monthly self-declaration of unemployment
apply_steps: Register on the Seva Sindhu portal or at Karnataka One / Bangalore One / Bapuji Seva Kendra | Submit education and domicile details | Verification by the department | Submit monthly self-declaration to keep receiving the allowance

name: Gruha Jyothi Scheme
short_description: Free domestic electricity in Karnataka up to your average usage plus a buffer, within 200 units a month.
full_description: Karnataka guarantee scheme giving domestic electricity consumers free power up to their 2022-23 average monthly consumption plus an allowance (10%, with later revisions for low consumers), subject to a ceiling of 200 units per month. Consumption above the entitlement is billed. Tenants can apply using the RR number of the premises.
ministry: Energy Department, Government of Karnataka
benefit_description: Zero bill for consumption within the household's entitled units (maximum 200 units per month).
documents: Electricity account ID / RR number | Aadhaar | Rental agreement or address proof (tenants)
apply_steps: Apply on the Seva Sindhu portal or at Karnataka One / Bangalore One / Grama One centres | Link Aadhaar with the electricity account (RR number) | Entitlement is applied automatically on monthly bills

name: Shakti Scheme (Free Bus Travel for Women)
short_description: Free travel for women and gender minorities domiciled in Karnataka on state-run non-AC buses.
full_description: Karnataka guarantee scheme allowing women (including girl students) and gender minorities domiciled in Karnataka to travel free on ordinary and express non-AC, non-luxury buses of KSRTC, BMTC, NWKRTC and KKRTC within the state. A Shakti smart card is issued; until then a government photo ID gets a zero-value ticket.
ministry: Transport Department, Government of Karnataka
benefit_description: Free intra-state travel on non-AC state transport buses.
documents: Aadhaar or other government photo ID showing Karnataka address
apply_steps: Apply for the Shakti smart card on the Seva Sindhu portal | Until issued, show a government photo ID to the conductor for a zero-value ticket

name: Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thogai
short_description: Rs 1,000 per month to women heads of family in Tamil Nadu with family income below Rs 2.5 lakh.
full_description: Tamil Nadu scheme paying Rs 1,000 per month to one woman (aged 21 or above) per ration card. Family annual income must be below Rs 2.5 lakh, landholding below 5 acres wet or 10 acres dry land, and annual household electricity consumption below 3,600 units. Excluded: income tax assessees, households owning a car or four-wheeler, government/PSU/bank employees and pensioners, and elected representatives.
ministry: Government of Tamil Nadu
benefit_description: Rs 1,000 per month by DBT.
documents: Ration card | Aadhaar | Bank account details | Electricity bill details
apply_steps: Collect and submit the application at the ration shop / special camp where your ration card is registered | Verification by revenue officials | Rejected applicants may file an appeal

name: Pudhumai Penn Scheme
short_description: Rs 1,000 per month for girls who studied Class 6-12 in Tamil Nadu government schools, during higher education.
full_description: Tamil Nadu scheme (Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance) paying Rs 1,000 per month to girl students who studied Class 6 to 12 in government, government-aided (Tamil medium) or local body schools in Tamil Nadu, until they complete their first UG degree, diploma, ITI or other recognised course. Not applicable to distance/open university students.
ministry: Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
benefit_description: Rs 1,000 per month by DBT until completion of higher education.
documents: Aadhaar | School certificates for Class 6-12 | Transfer certificate | Mark sheets | Bank passbook | Residence certificate
apply_steps: Join a recognised higher education course | Apply through your institution / the official portal | Institution verifies schooling records | Amount credited monthly to your bank account

name: Tamil Pudhalvan Scheme
short_description: Rs 1,000 per month for boys who studied Class 6-12 in Tamil Nadu government schools, during higher education.
full_description: Launched in August 2024, the scheme pays Rs 1,000 per month to boys who studied Class 6 to 12 in Tamil Nadu government schools (or Tamil medium in government-aided schools) and join a degree, diploma, ITI or polytechnic course in a recognised institution in Tamil Nadu.
ministry: Government of Tamil Nadu
benefit_description: Rs 1,000 per month by DBT during the course.
documents: Aadhaar | Class 6-12 school records | Admission proof | Bank account details
apply_steps: Join an eligible course | Apply via the UMIS portal through your college | College/university verifies and forwards | Amount credited to bank account

name: Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana
short_description: Rs 25,000 in six instalments from birth to graduation for girls in Uttar Pradesh families earning up to Rs 3 lakh.
full_description: Uttar Pradesh scheme supporting girl children through six staged instalments: birth (Rs 5,000), full immunisation (Rs 2,000), Class 1 admission (Rs 3,000), Class 6 (Rs 3,000), Class 9 (Rs 5,000) and graduation/2-year diploma admission after Class 10/12 (Rs 7,000). Family must be resident of UP with annual income up to Rs 3 lakh and at most two children; maximum two girls per family.
ministry: Department of Women Welfare, Government of Uttar Pradesh
benefit_description: Total Rs 25,000 in six milestone instalments.
documents: Residence proof (ration card / Aadhaar / voter ID / utility bill) | Family income certificate | Girl's birth certificate | Photograph of girl with parent | Bank account details | School admission proof (for later stages)
apply_steps: Register on mksy.up.gov.in | Fill the application for the applicable category | Upload documents | Verification by block/district officials | Instalment credited by DBT

name: Uttar Pradesh Old Age Pension (Vridhavastha Pension Yojana)
short_description: Monthly pension for destitute residents of Uttar Pradesh aged 60 and above within income limits.
full_description: State old age pension (with central NSAP share) for Uttar Pradesh residents aged 60 or above, with income up to Rs 46,080 (rural) or Rs 56,460 (urban), not receiving any other government pension. Pension is paid by DBT.
ministry: Social Welfare Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh
benefit_description: Monthly pension (reported as Rs 1,000 per month) paid by DBT; confirm current rate on the portal.
documents: Age certificate | Income certificate from Tehsildar | Aadhaar | Bank account | Residence proof | Photograph
apply_steps: Apply online at sspy-up.gov.in | Fill personal, income and bank details | Upload documents | Verification by BDO/SDM | Pension credited by DBT

name: Subhadra Yojana
short_description: Rs 10,000 a year (Rs 50,000 over five years) to eligible women aged 21-60 in Odisha.
full_description: Odisha government scheme (2024-25 to 2028-29) giving eligible women Rs 10,000 per year in two instalments of Rs 5,000 for five years. Women must be Odisha residents aged 21 to 60. Excluded: women from economically well-off families, government employees, income tax payers, and women already receiving Rs 1,500/month (Rs 18,000/year) or more under another government scheme.
ministry: Department of Women and Child Development and Mission Shakti, Government of Odisha
benefit_description: Rs 10,000 per year in two instalments of Rs 5,000, total Rs 50,000 over 5 years.
documents: Aadhaar | Ration card / NFSA or SFSS card | Aadhaar-seeded single-holder bank account | Mobile number
apply_steps: Apply on the Subhadra portal or at an Anganwadi centre / block office / Mo Seba Kendra | Complete Aadhaar e-KYC | Verification by officials | Instalments credited by DBT

name: Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana
short_description: Rs 6,000 a year from Maharashtra on top of PM-KISAN for farmer families.
full_description: Maharashtra government scheme (GR of 15 June 2023) giving PM-KISAN beneficiary farmer families in Maharashtra an additional Rs 6,000 per year in three instalments of Rs 2,000, making Rs 12,000 per year together with PM-KISAN. No separate application: eligibility follows PM-KISAN registration.
ministry: Agriculture Department, Government of Maharashtra
benefit_description: Rs 6,000 per year in three instalments of Rs 2,000 by DBT.
documents: PM-KISAN registration | Land records in the farmer's name | Aadhaar-linked bank account | Registered mobile number
apply_steps: Ensure you are a registered PM-KISAN beneficiary with Aadhaar-linked bank account and e-KYC done | Check beneficiary status on nsmny.mahait.org | Instalments credited automatically

name: Lek Ladki Yojana
short_description: Rs 1,01,000 in stages for girls born on or after 1 April 2023 in yellow/orange ration card families in Maharashtra.
full_description: Maharashtra scheme for one or two daughters born on or after 1 April 2023 in families holding yellow or orange ration cards. Instalments: Rs 5,000 at birth, Rs 6,000 at Class 1, Rs 7,000 at Class 6, Rs 8,000 at Class 11 and Rs 75,000 at age 18. Family income limit reported as Rs 1 lakh per year. In 2026 the process was simplified: online application on Aaple Sarkar with Aadhaar e-KYC, single application for all stages; new cases must apply within one year of birth.
ministry: Women and Child Development Department, Government of Maharashtra
benefit_description: Total Rs 1,01,000 in five instalments from birth to age 18.
documents: Girl's birth certificate | Yellow or orange ration card | Family income certificate | Aadhaar of girl and parents | Bank account details
apply_steps: Apply online on the Aaple Sarkar portal or through the Anganwadi centre | Complete Aadhaar e-KYC for the girl and parents | Verification by WCD officials | Instalments credited by DBT as milestones are reached

name: Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Anudan Yojana
short_description: Rs 1,500 per month for destitute persons under 65 in Maharashtra with family income up to Rs 21,000.
full_description: Maharashtra social assistance scheme for destitute persons below 65 years: orphans, persons with disabilities, persons with serious illnesses (TB, cancer, AIDS, leprosy), destitute widows and divorced women, farmers' widows and others. Family annual income must be up to Rs 21,000 (Rs 50,000 for persons with disabilities) or the family is on the BPL list. Assistance raised to Rs 1,500 per month via DBT from December 2024.
ministry: Social Justice and Special Assistance Department, Government of Maharashtra
benefit_description: Rs 1,500 per month by DBT.
documents: Age proof | Income certificate from Talathi/Tahsildar | Residence proof | Disability / medical certificate (where applicable) | Aadhaar | Bank account details
apply_steps: Apply on Aaple Sarkar or at the Tahsildar / Collector office | Submit income, age and category documents | Verification by the Tahsil-level committee | Assistance credited monthly by DBT

name: Mukhyamantri Vayoshri Yojana
short_description: One-time Rs 3,000 for senior citizens aged 65+ in Maharashtra to buy assistive devices.
full_description: Maharashtra scheme giving a lump sum of Rs 3,000 by DBT to senior citizens (65 years completed as of 31 December 2023) with family annual income within Rs 2 lakh, to purchase aids such as spectacles, hearing aids, walkers, wheelchairs and knee braces and to access yoga/wellness centres.
ministry: Social Justice and Special Assistance Department, Government of Maharashtra
benefit_description: Lump sum Rs 3,000 credited to Aadhaar-linked bank account.
documents: Aadhaar card (or enrolment receipt) | Aadhaar-linked bank passbook | Income certificate | Proof of eligibility (BPL ration card / old age pension proof / district certificate) | Self-declaration | Passport-size photograph
apply_steps: Apply on the official Vayoshri portal or at the district social welfare office | Submit Aadhaar and income documents | Verification by district authorities | Rs 3,000 credited by DBT

name: Deen Dayal Lado Lakshmi Yojana
short_description: Rs 2,100 per month for women aged 23+ in Haryana families with verified income up to Rs 1 lakh.
full_description: Haryana scheme launched on 25 September 2025 paying Rs 2,100 per month to every eligible woman (married or unmarried) aged 23 or above, from a family with income up to Rs 1 lakh per year as verified in the Family Information Database Repository (Parivar Pehchan Patra), and resident in Haryana for at least 15 years (husband's residence counts for women married into the state). No cap on number of women per family. Later changes (2026) reportedly route part of the payout into RD/FD savings and extend coverage to some mothers of high-scoring government school students.
ministry: Social Justice, Empowerment, SC and BC Welfare Department, Government of Haryana
benefit_description: Rs 2,100 per month by DBT (part may be deposited as compulsory savings).
documents: Family ID (Parivar Pehchan Patra) | Aadhaar | Bank account | Proof of 15 years residence in Haryana
apply_steps: Ensure family income is verified in Parivar Pehchan Patra | Apply through the Lado Lakshmi mobile app / official portal | Complete verification | Monthly amount credited by DBT

name: Namo Lakshmi Yojana
short_description: Rs 50,000 over four years for girls in Class 9-12 in Gujarat with family income below Rs 6 lakh.
full_description: Gujarat scheme to improve girls' secondary and higher secondary education. Girls in Class 9 to 12 in government, grant-in-aid and private schools (GSHSEB or CBSE) with family income below Rs 6 lakh receive Rs 500/month for 10 months in Class 9 and 10 plus Rs 10,000 after Class 10, and Rs 750/month for 10 months in Class 11 and 12 plus Rs 15,000 after Class 12 - Rs 50,000 in all. Girls on other scholarships remain eligible.
ministry: Education Department, Government of Gujarat
benefit_description: Total Rs 50,000 over Class 9-12, paid monthly and as board-exam completion amounts.
documents: Student Aadhaar | Parent Aadhaar | Family income certificate | Bank account details | Mobile number | School enrolment proof
apply_steps: Contact your school, which registers eligible girls | Submit Aadhaar, income certificate and bank details | Verification by the District Education Officer | Amount credited by DBT
